issues.t: Misfire and check engine light from failed ignition coils
issues.sym: Shaking at idle, hesitation or stumbling when accelerating, a flashing or steady check engine light, and misfire codes such as P0303 or P0304.
issues.why: The individual ignition coils on the 3.0L V6 fail often, many owners replacing several over the life of the van. It is the most reported engine repair for these years.
issues.next: Have the misfire code read to find which cylinder is affected. Replace the bad coil and that plug; if the van has high miles, doing all coils and plugs at once can save repeat visits.

issues.t: Cooling fan runs constantly or not at all
issues.sym: The radiator fans keep running after the engine is off, or they never come on and the temperature climbs in traffic.
issues.why: The cooling fan control module fails, a widely reported fault on these vans.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge. If the fans do not run, avoid idling in traffic and have the fan control module tested and replaced.

issues.t: Collapsed or cracked PCV hose causes rough idle
issues.sym: Rough or erratic idle, a hissing sound, and a check engine light, sometimes with lean codes.
issues.why: The rubber crankcase ventilation (PCV) hose softens with heat and collapses or cracks, creating a vacuum leak.
issues.next: Ask a shop to check the PCV hose and valve when diagnosing a rough idle.

issues.t: Oil leak from timing chain cover
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the engine and oily residue around the passenger-side front of the engine.
issues.why: The sealant and gaskets around the timing chain front cover harden with age and start to seep oil, usually past 90,000 miles.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level. A small seep can be watched, but a steady leak needs the cover resealed, which is labor-heavy.

issues.t: Oil pan gasket and front crank seal leak
issues.sym: Oil drips under the engine and oil coating the bottom of the oil pan.
issues.why: The oil pan gasket and front crankshaft seal wear out on high-mileage engines.
issues.next: Have the leak cleaned and traced so you fix the right seal. Keep the oil topped up in the meantime.

issues.t: Water pump leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips at the front of the engine, a sweet smell, and a falling coolant level.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out, commonly between about 85,000 and 125,000 miles on these vans.
issues.next: Have the cooling system pressure tested and the pump replaced before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Corroded rear heater coolant pipes
issues.sym: Coolant puddles under the middle of the van, a sweet smell, low coolant, or weak rear heat.
issues.why: Metal coolant pipes that run under the van to the rear heater rust through over time.
issues.next: Have the lines inspected from underneath. Fix leaks quickly, because losing coolant can overheat the engine.

issues.t: Radiator cracks and leaks
issues.sym: Coolant on the ground at the front, steam or a sweet smell, and the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The plastic radiator tanks crack with age and heat cycles.
issues.next: Do not keep driving if it is overheating. Replace the radiator and refill and bleed the cooling system.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or puffing sound from the engine, especially when cold, exhaust smell, and sometimes loss of power or an oxygen sensor code.
issues.why: The exhaust manifolds crack from repeated heating and cooling.
issues.next: Have it inspected. An exhaust leak near the engine can let fumes into the cabin, so do not delay.

issues.t: Stalling or erratic idle from idle air control valve
issues.sym: The idle speed hunts up and down, or the engine stalls when coming to a stop.
issues.why: The idle air control valve gets dirty or fails and can no longer hold the idle steady.
issues.next: Have it cleaned or replaced and check for vacuum leaks such as the PCV hose at the same time.

issues.t: Check engine light from oxygen sensor
issues.sym: Check engine light with an oxygen sensor code, and sometimes worse fuel economy.
issues.why: Oxygen sensors wear out with age and miles, and their heaters fail.
issues.next: Have the code read and the sensor tested. Replace only the sensor the code points to.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring between gears, harsh shifts or the van not moving in drive or reverse.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic used in the early second-generation MPV is known for transmission problems, as the same gearbox has been in other Mazda and Ford models.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and condition. Have the transmission inspected and serviced early; if it is already slipping badly, a rebuild or replacement is likely.

issues.t: Jerky or harsh downshifts
issues.sym: Rough or jerky shifts, especially when slowing down, and sometimes the overdrive light coming on.
issues.why: Owners report shift quality problems on the 5-speed automatic, and dealers reprogrammed the computer software on many vans to fix shift feel.
issues.next: Ask a Mazda dealer whether a software update applies to your van, and have the fluid level and condition checked.

issues.t: Rotten-egg smell and failing catalytic converter
issues.sym: A sulfur or rotten-egg smell, sometimes inside the cabin, and a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners of 2000-2001 MPVs report catalytic converters that fail or give off a strong sulfur smell.
issues.next: Have the exhaust and converter checked. Any exhaust smell inside the van should be fixed quickly because of carbon monoxide risk.

issues.t: Worn engine and transmission mounts
issues.sym: Clunks when shifting into drive or reverse, extra vibration at idle, or the engine rocking when you accelerate.
issues.why: The rubber in the engine and transmission mounts breaks down with age.
issues.next: Have the mounts inspected with the engine running and in gear. Replace any that are torn.

issues.t: Power sliding door not working properly
issues.sym: The power sliding door stops partway, will not open or close by itself, or makes noise when moving.
issues.why: The drive module that moves the power sliding door can fail. Mazda published a service bulletin on removing and installing the power sliding door drive module for 2002-2005 MPVs.
issues.next: Make sure nothing is blocking the track, then have a dealer or shop diagnose the door. You can usually still operate it by hand.

issues.t: Takata passenger airbag inflator (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptoms. In a crash, the passenger airbag inflator could rupture and throw metal fragments.
issues.why: The Takata inflator propellant breaks down after years of heat and humidity. Mazda recalled 2004-2006 MPVs and later recalled vans again whose replacement inflators used the same design (campaigns including 18V402, 18V404 and 19V781).
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls and have a Mazda dealer replace the inflator for free as soon as possible.

issues.t: Fuel leak at injectors and fire risk (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell under the hood or fuel wetness around the intake.
issues.why: On some vans with engines from Ford's Cleveland plant, the fuel injectors did not match the lower intake manifold, which could leak fuel and start a fire. Mazda recalled them (campaign 99V171).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you smell fuel, stop driving and have it checked. Confirm the recall was done.

issues.t: Rear door may not latch with child lock on (recall)
issues.sym: A rear sliding door with the child lock set might not lock fully and could open while driving.
issues.why: Dust could jam the rear door lock linkage. Mazda recalled vans to install revised latch parts (campaign 99V191).
issues.next: Confirm the recall was done. Until it is, make sure the doors are fully closed and locked before moving.

issues.t: Brake line layout on vans without ABS (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving. If one brake circuit failed, stopping distance would be longer than allowed.
issues.why: On MPVs without anti-lock brakes, the brake pipe layout did not meet the federal standard for stopping with a partial brake failure. Mazda recalled them to modify the brake system (campaign 01V382).
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard, press it much harder than normal. If it sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Have a dealer confirm the brake modification was done on your van.

issues.t: Fog light socket can fall out and burn bumper (recall)
issues.sym: A burning plastic smell from the front bumper, or a fog light that stops working.
issues.why: The fog light bulb socket could work loose from its housing and drop into the bumper, where the hot bulb could melt or burn it. Mazda recalled vans with fog lights (campaigns 03V053 and 03V206).
issues.next: If a fog light stops working or you smell burning, switch the fog lights off and have a dealer check the recall.

issues.t: Ignition switch can overheat and smoke (recall)
issues.sym: Smoke or a burning smell from the steering column when starting, or the starter stays engaged after the engine starts.
issues.why: Grease inside the ignition switch can carbonize and let current flow between the contacts, overheating the switch. Mazda recalled 1989-1998 MPVs (campaign 15V674).
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. If you notice smoke or the starter keeps running, stop driving and contact a Mazda dealer to have the free replacement switch fitted.

issues.t: Lifter ticking after a cold start
issues.sym: A ticking or tapping noise from the top of the engine for a short time after a cold start.
issues.why: The hydraulic lash adjusters (lifters) take a moment to fill with oil and can tick until they do. Mazda issued bulletins on this noise.
issues.next: Use the correct oil grade and change it on time. If the noise lasts after warm-up, have the lifters checked.

issues.t: Timing belt tensioner pulley wear
issues.sym: A whine or rattle from the front of the engine; after a timing belt job, some vans had a no-start, rough idle or low power.
issues.why: Mazda issued bulletins telling dealers to inspect or replace the timing belt tensioner pulley at the 60,000-mile service, and another for problems after a timing belt replacement.
issues.next: Replace the timing belt, tensioner and idler pulleys together on schedule, and make sure the belt timing marks are set correctly.

issues.t: Transmission slips from low fluid level
issues.sym: The van slips or is slow to engage in drive and reverse.
issues.why: Mazda issued a service bulletin (005/97K) for slipping in forward and reverse caused by a low automatic transmission fluid level.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level with the engine warm and running. Top up with the correct fluid and look for leaks.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working
issues.sym: The wipers stop partway or quit, then may come back later.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin (003/97G) for wiper motors that stop because the circuit breaker in the motor trips.
issues.next: Have the wiper motor and linkage checked. A binding linkage can make the breaker trip.

issues.t: Front power windows chatter or grind
issues.sym: Chattering, grinding or squeaking from the front doors when the windows go up or down.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin (02198) for this noise from the front power window mechanism.
issues.next: Have the window tracks cleaned and lubricated; replace the regulator if it is worn.

issues.t: Water leaks from sunroof
issues.sym: Water dripping from the headliner or wet carpets after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Mazda issued a bulletin (00398) for water leaks from the sliding sunroof, usually from the seal or clogged drain tubes.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drain tubes and check the seal. Dry the interior quickly to prevent mold.
